title: Staggered device firmware + runtime rollout with autoscaler contract
creator: Priya Menon
description: Summary: Design and implement a staggered rollout mechanism that coordinates firmware/runtime upgrades for Dedicated GPU pools with the cluster autoscaler and tenant-aware routing. The goal is to avoid capacity cliffs during upgrades by establishing an autoscaler contract, temporary admission controls, and a traffic smoothing layer that reduces headroom pressure.
background: We've seen an increase in upgrade-induced capacity pressure when LTS channel upgrades and driver/firmware updates trigger node restarts across dedicated pools. Existing drain-and-wait flows rely on conservative timeouts and manual pacing. This ticket prototypes an automated, contract-based handshake between the upgrade orchestrator and the autoscaler that ensures drained nodes are replenished before new drains proceed.
proposal: 1) Introduce an autoscaler contract API: upgrade controller signals required replacement capacity and desired stabilization window. 2) Implement staged device groups: split a pool into N slices and apply rolling upgrades to one slice at a time with configurable overlap. 3) Admission smoothing: temporarily reduce new admission velocity for latency-sensitive tenants when pool headroom drops below thresholds. 4) Observability + rollback: add rollout gates with monitored SLOs (p99 latency, queue depth, allocation failures) and automated rollback on threshold breaches.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes 'autoscaler_contract' endpoint and can report desired replacement_count and stabilization_window
A pool can be configured with slice_count and slice_order for staged upgrades via pool annotations
During a slice upgrade, cluster autoscaler performs capacity provisioning within the stabilization_window at >95% success rate in test clusters
Admission smoothing triggers when available GPU slots < 15% and reduces new mx-concurrency by configured factor
Dashboards show per-slice rollout metrics: drained_nodes, replacements_pending, SLO_violations, rollback_reason
Canary rollout on test pool completes without >5% application-level error increase and rollback if SLO breach occurs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler overshoot causing unnecessary cost — Mitigation: cap replacement_count to tenant reservations and short-circuit if preemptible capacity available
Risk: Throttling latency-sensitive tenants degrades UX — Mitigation: per-tenant QoS exemptions and canary thresholds before broad application
Risk: Firmware incompatibility discovered post-upgrade — Mitigation: staged rollouts with fast rollback and automated health checks (driver probe + smoke inference)
Risk: Race between autoscaler and drain leads to double-provisioning — Mitigation: idempotent contract ack and lease semantics for replacement slots
implementation_notes: Autoscaler contract will be implemented as a Kubernetes CRD 'UpgradeContract' that the autoscaler watches; fields: desired_replacements, stabilization_window, slice_id
Upgrade controller schedules slice drains based on slice_order and awaits contract_acks from autoscaler before proceeding
Admission smoothing implemented as a rate-limiter middleware in the request router with per-tenant tokens adjustable at runtime
Add feature flag 'staggered-rollout-v2' to gate behavior in runtime and Dedicated control plane
Create migration job to annotate existing pools with default slice_count=4 and safe_timeouts to avoid immediate churn
work_items: Design autoscaler_contract CRD and gRPC shim for existing autoscaler
Implement slice-based scheduler in upgrade controller
Add admission smoothing middleware and config API
Build dashboards and alerts for rollout gates and SLOs
End-to-end canary run on staging Dedicated pool
Author runbook and rollback playbook for on-call
